pages.text: An excited atom struck by a photon of just the right energy gives off a second, identical photon: $(thing)stimulated emission$(). Fill a crystal with excited atoms, put it between two mirrors, and the light builds on itself.

A garnet boule grown with a rare earth is the crystal: neodymium in garnet lases at 1064 nm, in the infrared. Cut it along its lattice into $(item)Laser Rods$(); with mirrors, silica lenses and a flash to pump it, it becomes a $(item)Laser Head$().
Behind it sits a $(item)Faraday Isolator$(): garnet in a strong magnetic field turns polarised light the same way going and coming, so its own reflection cannot get back into the laser and upset it.
